sentences.text: Llovió toda la noche, y a la mañana siguiente el camino de la aldea estaba lleno de barro.
sentences.english: It rained all night, and the next morning the village road was full of mud.

sentences.text: Doña Marta miró por la ventana de su cocina y movió la cabeza.
sentences.english: Doña Marta looked out of her kitchen window and shook her head.

sentences.text: —Con este barro nadie va a poder salir hoy —dijo.
sentences.english: "With this mud nobody is going to be able to go out today," she said.

sentences.text: Pero su nieto Nico, que tenía diez años, ya se estaba poniendo los zapatos.
sentences.english: But her grandson Nico, who was ten, was already putting on his shoes.

sentences.text: —Yo sí puedo salir, abuela.
sentences.english: "I can go out, Grandma."

sentences.text: —No le tengo miedo al barro.
sentences.english: "I am not afraid of mud."

sentences.text: Salió de la casa y empezó a caminar por el camino, mirando todo.
sentences.english: He left the house and began to walk along the road, looking at everything.

sentences.text: Buscaba algo, pero no sabía qué.
sentences.english: He was looking for something, but he did not know what.

sentences.text: Cerca del árbol grande, vio algo pequeño debajo del barro.
sentences.english: Near the big tree, he saw something small under the mud.

sentences.text: Metió la mano y sacó una llave.
sentences.english: He put his hand in and pulled out a key.

sentences.text: Era una llave grande y vieja, oscura por el barro y muy fría.
sentences.english: It was a big, old key, dark with mud and very cold.

sentences.text: La limpió con su camisa y la miró por todos lados.
sentences.english: He wiped it on his shirt and looked at it from every side.

sentences.text: «¿De quién es esta llave?», pensó.
sentences.english: "Whose key is this?" he thought.

sentences.text: Nadie en la aldea tenía una llave tan grande.
sentences.english: Nobody in the village had such a big key.

sentences.text: Sin pensar más, corrió a su casa.
sentences.english: Without thinking any more, he ran home.

sentences.text: Doña Marta estaba en la cocina, preparando el desayuno, cuando Nico entró corriendo.
sentences.english: Doña Marta was in the kitchen, making breakfast, when Nico came in running.

sentences.text: —Abuela, mire lo que encontré —dijo él, sin poder hablar bien.
sentences.english: "Grandma, look what I found," he said, hardly able to speak.

sentences.text: Ella se dio vuelta con una taza en la mano, vio la llave, y la taza cayó al piso.
sentences.english: She turned around with a cup in her hand, saw the key, and the cup fell to the floor.

sentences.text: Doña Marta no dijo nada.
sentences.english: Doña Marta said nothing.

sentences.text: Tenía la cara blanca, y se sentó en una silla de la cocina.
sentences.english: Her face was white, and she sat down on a kitchen chair.

sentences.text: —¿Dónde la encontraste? —preguntó por fin, con una voz muy baja.
sentences.english: "Where did you find it?" she finally asked, in a very low voice.

sentences.text: —En el camino, abuela, cerca del árbol grande.
sentences.english: "On the road, Grandma, near the big tree."

sentences.text: —¿Por qué?
sentences.english: "Why?"

sentences.text: —¿Es de alguien?
sentences.english: "Does it belong to someone?"

sentences.text: —Es mía —dijo ella.
sentences.english: "It is mine," she said.

sentences.text: —Es la llave de la casa de mis padres.
sentences.english: "It is the key to my parents' house."

sentences.text: —¿Esa casa del final del camino?
sentences.english: "That house at the end of the road?"

sentences.text: —¡Pero si está cerrada desde siempre!
sentences.english: "But it has always been closed!"

sentences.text: —Está cerrada desde hace cuarenta años —contestó ella.
sentences.english: "It has been closed for forty years," she answered.

sentences.text: —Y yo perdí esta llave cuando tenía veinte.
sentences.english: "And I lost this key when I was twenty."

sentences.text: —¿Y cómo volvió?
sentences.english: "And how did it come back?"

sentences.text: —La lluvia, a veces, devuelve las cosas.
sentences.english: "The rain, sometimes, gives things back."

sentences.text: Nico se quedó mirándola.
sentences.english: Nico stood looking at her.

sentences.text: Nunca había visto a su abuela así, tan callada y tan pequeña.
sentences.english: He had never seen his grandmother like this, so quiet and so small.

sentences.text: Después de desayunar, doña Marta se levantó de la silla y tomó la llave.
sentences.english: After having breakfast, doña Marta got up from the chair and took the key.

sentences.text: —Vamos —dijo.
sentences.english: "Let us go," she said.

sentences.text: —Hay cosas que uno guarda cuarenta años porque tiene miedo de mirarlas otra vez.
sentences.english: "There are things that one keeps for forty years because one is afraid to look at them again."

sentences.text: Salieron juntos por el camino, ella despacio y él con la llave en el bolsillo.
sentences.english: They went out together along the road, she slowly and he with the key in his pocket.

sentences.text: —Abuela, ¿tiene miedo? —preguntó Nico.
sentences.english: "Grandma, are you afraid?" Nico asked.

sentences.text: —No —dijo ella.
sentences.english: "No," she said.

sentences.text: Y después, con una sonrisa, dijo: —Bueno, un poco.
sentences.english: And then, with a smile, she said, "Well, a little."

sentences.text: Mientras caminaban, ella le contó la historia.
sentences.english: While they walked, she told him the story.

sentences.text: Su papá, don Tomás, había sido el hombre más alegre de la aldea.
sentences.english: Her father, don Tomás, had been the happiest man in the village.

sentences.text: Cada noche tocaba la guitarra en la cocina, y toda la familia se quedaba escuchando esa música.
sentences.english: Every night he played the guitar in the kitchen, and the whole family stayed listening to that music.

sentences.text: Una noche de invierno, él se enfermó y no se levantó más.
sentences.english: One winter night he got sick and did not get up again.

sentences.text: Marta tenía veinte años y trabajaba en la ciudad, y llegó tarde.
sentences.english: Marta was twenty and worked in the city, and she arrived late.

sentences.text: Cuando su papá se murió, ella cerró la puerta de la casa con esta llave y se la guardó en el bolsillo.
sentences.english: When her father died, she closed the door of the house with this key and put it in her pocket.

sentences.text: —Pero esa misma semana, cuando volvía a la ciudad, la llave se me cayó en el barro —dijo ella.
sentences.english: "But that same week, when I was going back to the city, the key fell into the mud," she said.

sentences.text: —Y yo no la busqué.
sentences.english: "And I did not look for it."

sentences.text: —¿Por qué no?
sentences.english: "Why not?"

sentences.text: —Porque era más fácil no volver.
sentences.english: "Because it was easier not to go back."

sentences.text: —¿Todavía le duele, abuela?
sentences.english: "Does it still hurt, Grandma?"

sentences.text: —Todavía —dijo ella.
sentences.english: "Still," she said.

sentences.text: —Pero ya no tanto como antes.
sentences.english: "But not so much as before."

sentences.text: La casa estaba al final del camino, entre dos árboles grandes.
sentences.english: The house stood at the end of the road, between two big trees.

sentences.text: Tenía las ventanas cerradas y la puerta cubierta de polvo.
sentences.english: Its windows were closed and its door was covered with dust.

sentences.text: Doña Marta puso la llave en la puerta, pero la llave no se movía.
sentences.english: Doña Marta put the key in the door, but the key would not move.

sentences.text: —Déjeme probar, abuela —dijo Nico.
sentences.english: "Let me try, Grandma," said Nico.

sentences.text: Con las dos manos, tiró muy fuerte, y la puerta se abrió con un golpe.
sentences.english: With both hands he pulled very hard, and the door opened with a bang.

sentences.text: Adentro estaba oscuro, y todo olía a polvo y a tiempo.
sentences.english: Inside it was dark, and everything smelled of dust and time.

sentences.text: —Cuidado —dijo ella.
sentences.english: "Careful," she said.

sentences.text: —El piso está viejo.
sentences.english: "The floor is old."

sentences.text: Entraron despacio, uno después del otro.
sentences.english: They went in slowly, one after the other.

sentences.text: Nico corrió a la ventana más próxima y la abrió.
sentences.english: Nico ran to the nearest window and opened it.

sentences.text: La luz entró de golpe y llenó todo el cuarto.
sentences.english: The light came in all at once and filled the whole room.

sentences.text: Vieron la mesa, las tazas, y sobre la mesa, una foto de la familia.
sentences.english: They saw the table, the cups, and on the table a photo of the family.

sentences.text: —¿Quién es esa niña de la foto? —preguntó Nico.
sentences.english: "Who is that girl in the photo?" asked Nico.

sentences.text: —Soy yo, a los diez años —dijo ella.
sentences.english: "It is me, at ten years old," she said.

sentences.text: —Y ese señor alegre es mi papá.
sentences.english: "And that cheerful man is my father."

sentences.text: Al lado de la ventana había una silla vieja, y contra la silla, una guitarra cubierta de polvo.
sentences.english: Next to the window there was an old chair, and against the chair a guitar covered with dust.

sentences.text: —Esa era la silla de mi papá —dijo doña Marta, con la voz rota.
sentences.english: "That was my father's chair," said doña Marta, her voice breaking.

sentences.text: —Y esa es su guitarra.
sentences.english: "And that is his guitar."

sentences.text: —Nadie la tocó en cuarenta años.
sentences.english: "Nobody has played it in forty years."

sentences.text: Nico la tomó con mucho cuidado.
sentences.english: Nico took it with great care.

sentences.text: —¿Puedo tocarla?
sentences.english: "May I play it?"

sentences.text: —Mi papá decía que una guitarra que nadie toca se muere —contestó ella.
sentences.english: "My father used to say that a guitar nobody plays dies," she answered.

sentences.text: —Tocá.
sentences.english: "Play."

sentences.text: Nico pasó los dedos por las cuerdas, y la guitarra sonó.
sentences.english: Nico ran his fingers over the strings, and the guitar sounded.

sentences.text: No era una música bonita, porque las cuerdas estaban viejas.
sentences.english: It was not pretty music, because the strings were old.

sentences.text: Pero a doña Marta se le llenaron los ojos.
sentences.english: But doña Marta's eyes filled up.

sentences.text: —¿Escuchás cómo suena? —dijo con voz suave.
sentences.english: "Do you hear how it sounds?" she said in a soft voice.

sentences.text: —Es la misma música.
sentences.english: "It is the same music."

sentences.text: —Es la música de mi casa.
sentences.english: "It is the music of my home."

sentences.text: Cerró los ojos un momento.
sentences.english: She closed her eyes for a moment.

sentences.text: Después abrió las otras ventanas, una por una.
sentences.english: Then she opened the other windows, one by one.

sentences.text: —No voy a cerrar esta casa otra vez —dijo.
sentences.english: "I am not going to close this house again," she said.

sentences.text: —Alguien tiene que vivir aquí.
sentences.english: "Someone has to live here."

sentences.text: —Podemos venir cada sábado —dijo Nico.
sentences.english: "We can come every Saturday," said Nico.

sentences.text: —Yo limpio, y usted me cuenta algo de su papá.
sentences.english: "I clean, and you tell me something about your father."

sentences.text: —Y vos tocás la guitarra —dijo ella.
sentences.english: "And you play the guitar," she said.

sentences.text: —Pero primero hay que cambiar esas cuerdas.
sentences.english: "But first those strings have to be changed."

sentences.text: Esa tarde bajaron por el camino con la guitarra, y los vecinos salieron a mirar.
sentences.english: That afternoon they came down the road with the guitar, and the neighbors came out to look.

sentences.text: —¿Qué llevan ahí? —preguntó alguien.
sentences.english: "What are you carrying there?" someone asked.

sentences.text: —Una historia —contestó doña Marta, y se rió.
sentences.english: "A story," answered doña Marta, and she laughed.

sentences.text: El sábado siguiente, Nico llevó cuerdas nuevas y limpió la guitarra con mucho cuidado.
sentences.english: The following Saturday, Nico brought new strings and cleaned the guitar very carefully.

sentences.text: Esa noche, sentada en una silla en el patio, doña Marta oyó música otra vez.
sentences.english: That night, sitting on a chair in the patio, doña Marta heard music again.

sentences.text: Nadie en la aldea había oído esa guitarra desde hacía cuarenta años, y los vecinos se sentaron a escuchar.
sentences.english: Nobody in the village had heard that guitar in forty years, and the neighbors sat down to listen.

sentences.text: Desde ese día, doña Marta y Nico fueron a la casa vieja cada sábado.
sentences.english: From that day on, doña Marta and Nico went to the old house every Saturday.

sentences.text: Ella lavó las ventanas y las tazas, y él practicó en la silla de don Tomás hasta que le dolieron los dedos.
sentences.english: She washed the windows and the cups, and he practiced on don Tomás's chair until his fingers hurt.

sentences.text: Al principio la música sonaba mal, y los vecinos se reían, pero nadie se iba.
sentences.english: At first the music sounded bad, and the neighbors laughed, but nobody left.

sentences.text: Poco a poco, la casa dejó de ser un lugar oscuro y cerrado.
sentences.english: Little by little, the house stopped being a dark, closed place.

sentences.text: Doña Marta ya no tenía miedo de entrar.
sentences.english: Doña Marta was no longer afraid to go in.

sentences.text: A veces, cuando Nico tocaba una canción que ella conocía, cerraba los ojos y cantaba bajito.
sentences.english: Sometimes, when Nico played a song she knew, she closed her eyes and sang softly.

sentences.text: La llave ya no estaba en el bolsillo de nadie.
sentences.english: The key was no longer in anybody's pocket.

sentences.text: Doña Marta la guardó en un clavo, al lado de la puerta de su cocina, para verla cada mañana.
sentences.english: Doña Marta hung it on a nail by her kitchen door, to see it every morning.

sentences.text: La llave volvió, pero lo que volvió de verdad fue la música.
sentences.english: The key came back, but what really came back was the music.
